title: Closed graph and universal closedness of a relative self-product
statement: Let $A,B,C$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $p:A\to B$, $q:C\to B$ and $f:A\to C$ satisfying $q\circ f=p$. Assume that $p$ is universally closed and $q$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Write $P=A\times_B C$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $\pi_A,\pi_C$, and let $\Gamma_f=(\mathrm{id}_A,f):A\to P$. The square with top arrow $f:A\to C$, bottom arrow $(f\circ\pi_A,\pi_C):P\to C\times_B C$, left arrow $\Gamma_f$ and right arrow the diagonal $\Delta_q:C\to C\times_B C$ is cartesian. Moreover $\Gamma_f$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $f=\pi_C\circ\Gamma_f$ is universally closed, and $p_2=p\circ\operatorname{pr}_1:A\times_C A\to B$ is universally closed. For every scheme $T$ and morphism $h:T\to B$, the induced morphism $f_T:A\times_B T\to C\times_B T$ is universally closed. In particular the underlying maps of $p$ and $p_2$ send closed subsets to closed subsets.

mathlib_match.how: One direct Mathlib application per clause, read 2026-10-23. Use p = f ≫ q (Lean writes composition left to right); HasPullbacks Scheme supplies every pullback. (1) CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback_lift_diagonal_isPullback f q, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Shapes/Diagonal.lean:396-399, is exactly the square: its four arrows are f, pullback.lift (𝟙 A) f, pullback.diagonal q, and pullback.map (f ≫ q) q q q f (𝟙 C) (𝟙 B). The latter has components f ∘ π_A and π_C, so rewriting f ≫ q = p gives the stated square, with no separatedness hypothesis needed. (2) AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.instIsClosedImmersionLiftSchemeId, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Separated.lean:138-139, gives the closed immersion of this same graph from IsSeparated q. (3) The factorization is CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift_snd, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Shapes/Pullback/HasPullback.lean:180-181. Universal closedness of f is AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed.of_comp_of_isSeparated f q, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Proper.lean:111-113, after rewriting f ≫ q = p. (4) For p_2, AlgebraicGeometry.universallyClosedTypeComp (pullback.fst f f) p, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/UniversallyClosed.lean:87-89, applies directly: its first instance is universallyClosed_fst f f at lines 95-97 with the UniversallyClosed f of (3), and the other is the hypothesis UniversallyClosed p. No properness or finite-type assumption is used. (5) For each h:T ⟶ B, CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.pullbackLift_fst_snd (P := @AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed) h (show p = f ≫ q from the given equality) (the UniversallyClosed f of (3)), Mathlib/CategoryTheory/MorphismProperty/Limits.lean:231-235, gives exactly f_T with components f ∘ pr_A and pr_T. The required instance universallyClosed_isStableUnderBaseChange is Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/UniversallyClosed.lean:65-66. (6) AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isClosedMap, Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/UniversallyClosed.lean:49-50, applied separately to p and p_2 gives the final two closed-map claims. This is a collection of Mathlib clauses, not an identification between different notions; def-weil-proper-morphism and def-pc-fibre-product already match IsSeparated, UniversallyClosed and pullback.
